resources.string: Show USB state
Show tethering state
Call a real number you can talk to (another phone or a voicemail). Answer each step during the call.
Show call state
Place the call. It connects and the call timer runs.
You hear the other side clearly in the earpiece.
The other side hears you clearly.
Speakerphone: both directions still work.
Mute stops the other side hearing you, unmute restores it.
With a wired or Bluetooth headset, call audio goes through it.
Check rild and binder waits
Receive an incoming call: it rings and can be answered.
Do not dial a real emergency number to test this. Only place a real call if your emergency service or carrier offers a test procedure.
The lock screen shows an Emergency call button and it opens the emergency dialer.
With a SIM: the dialer recognizes the local emergency number (it shows the emergency call styling as you type it, do not press call).
Without a SIM: the status bar or lock screen shows \"Emergency calls only\" when a network is in range.
Show emergency numbers
Read the emergency numbers the device knows
You need a SIM with SMS and mobile data, and another phone. MMS needs mobile data on, even when Wi-Fi is connected.
Send an SMS to the other phone: it arrives.
Reply from the other phone: the SMS arrives here and shows a notification.
Send a picture message (MMS): it arrives with the picture.
Receive a picture message: it downloads and the picture shows.
Use a SIM whose carrier offers VoLTE and Wi-Fi calling. Turn both on in the SIM settings first.
Show carrier IMS config
Read the carrier IMS settings
Show IMS registration
IMS is registered: the status bar or SIM status shows VoLTE, or the state below names IMS.
Place a call on LTE with Wi-Fi off: it connects without falling back to 2G or 3G, and data keeps working during the call.
Turn on airplane mode, then Wi-Fi only, and place a Wi-Fi call: it connects and audio works both ways.
Skip the parts stock does not support. You need two SIMs, or one SIM and an eSIM profile.
Show SIM slots
Read the SIM slot setup
With both SIMs in: each one registers and shows its own signal.
Calls, SMS and mobile data work on SIM 1, then on SIM 2 after switching the defaults.
With only a physical SIM, then only an eSIM: calls, SMS and data work on each.
Adding or deleting an eSIM profile works from the SIM settings.
You need mobile data, or Ethernet, as the upstream, and a second device.
Turn on the Wi-Fi hotspot.
The hotspot appears as tethered
Another device connects to the hotspot and can browse.
Connect the phone to a computer with a data cable. Mobile data must be the upstream.
Switch USB to tethering
Turn on USB tethering (via Shizuku or the settings screen).
The computer gets a network interface and can browse.
Repeat on every other USB port with data (if the device has several).
Pair a computer or another phone first.
Turn on Bluetooth tethering.
The paired device connects through Bluetooth and can browse.
Connect the phone to a computer with a data cable.
Switch USB to MTP
Switch USB to file transfer.
The computer shows the phone storage.
Copy a file from the computer to the phone and back.
Repeat on every other USB port.
You need an OTG adapter (or a USB-C drive) and, for the second part, a USB Ethernet adapter.
Show volumes
Plug a USB drive in: it mounts and its files open.
Copy a file to the drive, eject it from the notification, and the file is there on a computer.
Show interfaces
Plug a USB Ethernet adapter with a cable: the device gets network and can browse with Wi-Fi off.
FM needs wired headphones as the antenna.
Plug wired headphones in.
Open the FM radio app and tune to a local station.
You hear the station, and switching to speaker works.
This erases the SD card. Use a card with nothing you need.
Format the card as internal (phone) storage.
Move an app or data to the card and the app still opens.
Reboot: the card mounts again and the moved app still works.
Show storage volumes
Needs a newer build published for this device (official or your own update server).
Show version
Current version
The Updater lists available builds.
Download and install an update: the device reboots into the new build with data kept.
Rebooting closes this app. Save this test after coming back.
Reboot to recovery now
Reboot to recovery (or use the key combo).
The recovery documented for this ROM starts (LineageOS Recovery on LineageOS-based builds).
\"Apply update > Apply from ADB\" accepts an adb sideload of the build zip.
The device boots normally afterwards.
Use the add-ons the ROM documents for this device (for example a Google apps package).
Each documented add-on sideloads in recovery without errors.
The device boots and the add-on works.
Turn off Pointer location at the end if you turn it on.
Turn on Pointer location
Turn on Pointer location.
Put 5 fingers down and move them: the top bar counts every finger and each trail follows its finger.
Swipe along every edge and corner: the trail never jumps or breaks.
Leave the screen untouched for a minute, including while charging: no touch appears by itself.
Turn off Pointer location
Turn Pointer location off.
Rebooting closes this app. Save this test after coming back.
Power the device off, then plug in a charger: a charging animation or battery level shows.
The level rises after a while, and the device boots normally with the power button.
Skip a cable the device cannot use. Use a known good charger and cable for each.
Show battery state
Charge from a USB-A charger: the device shows charging and the current is positive.
Charge from a USB-C charger with a C-to-C cable: the device shows charging, at the stock speed if the charger supports it.
This erases all data, including this app and its results. Pull the report first, reinstall the app after setup, then record this test.
Run the factory reset from settings.
The device reboots, wipes and boots into the setup wizard.
Show encryption state
Setup completes and the device is still encrypted.
On a fresh install, before signing in to a Google account.
Open microG settings and run the self-check: every item is ticked.
Exposure Notifications is off by default.
Advanced Privacy ships with every /e/OS build.
Advanced Privacy is reachable from the privacy settings and its dashboard opens.
Needs network access and Play Integrity API Checker from App Lounge. Connect Shizuku and the app runs the check and reads the verdict for you.
Install Play Integrity API Checker from App Lounge once. The app then opens it, runs the check and reads the verdict through Shizuku. Keep the phone unlocked while it runs.
Open in App Lounge
Run the check
Running…
Install Play Integrity API Checker from App Lounge and open it.
Run the check: it reports MEETS_BASIC_INTEGRITY. Device and strong integrity are not expected.
Extra Dim once got stuck on. Toggle it from Quick Settings and check the setting follows.
Read Extra Dim state
Turn Extra Dim on from Quick Settings: the screen gets dimmer.
Turn it off: brightness comes back and the state reads 0.
Repeat on and off 3 times: it never gets stuck.
Read Night Light state
Night Light turns on and off the same way.
Let the device idle overnight with the screen off before the drain steps.
Screen off and on 20 times: it always wakes, never stays black.
Show discharge stats
Overnight idle drain is in line with stock (roughly 1 %% per hour or less).
Show wake locks
No app or service holds the device awake.
